### Plugin Type

VSCode Extension

When using deep-planning mode, for languages with dependencies in project folder, the find commands issued by Cline will include results from dependencies, I believe this is unintended. linked_prs.title: fix #6172: `detectedShell` returns non-string on some Windows machines leading to API request hanging
linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6204 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6203 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6202 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6172 - https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/6159 - https://www.reddit.com/r/CLine/comments/1nfkxep/cline_3282_stuck_at_loading/ ### Description Slack dump: The user reported that API Request is stuck at 'Loading...'. The order of events for a first request in task/index is `recursivelyMakeClineRequests` -> `api_req_started` "Loading..." -> `ensureCheckpointInitialized` -> `this.checkpointManager.commit()` -> `loadContext` I'm assuming that checkpoints are not the issue here since they timeout after 15s and the user reported the request hangs infinitely while on old versions it doesnt. I investigated the loadContext function and compared the diff of v3.26.6 and 3.28 - some change that was made here that was the cause of the issue. The github issue showed the error "toLowerCase is not a function" so something in loadContext eventually calls this function on an object that isn't a string. the trace is loadContext -> Promise.all -> Promise.all The only flow where a second promise.all is called is when processUserContent is called in loadContext, which calls parseMentions and parseSlashCommands. I believe one of these two functions is causing the failure/hang ie we now pass in this.focusChainSettings to the parseSlashCommands function Eventually I traced the error to this: ``` isPowerShell = detectedShell != null && typeof detectedShell === "string" && (detectedShell.toLowerCase().includes("powershell") || detectedShell.toLowerCase().includes("pwsh")) ``` - the bug only happened to people on windows - and it happened in loadcontext -> parseslashcommands - and the new changes here were the deepplanning stuff ### Test Procedure I pulled up a diff from v3.27 and v3.28 and found that we made some changes to parseSlashCommands in loadContext. Unable to reproduce the issue myself, but considering this was only reported by Windows users and the trace led to `loadContext` -> `parseSlashCommands` was the only thing that changed, and that the change had to do with detecting if the user used powershell, and the error being thrown was 'toLowerCase' not existing, makes me very certain this was the issue. ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [ ] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [ ] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [ ] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Fixes issue in `deepPlanningToolResponse` where `detectedShell` could return a non-string, causing API requests to hang on Windows. > > - **Bug Fix**: > - Fixes issue in `deepPlanningToolResponse` in `commands.ts` where `detectedShell` could return a non-string value on some Windows machines, causing API requests to hang. > - Ensures `detectedShell` is a string before calling `toLowerCase` to prevent errors. > - **Error Handling**: > - Adds a try-catch block around the logic to determine if `detectedShell` is PowerShell. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 4b216d6d5776596d02f69a0f285e567c820dd2b4. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/cline/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed.

linked_prs.title: fix: sap provider - support gpt-5 family in orchestration mode
linked_prs.body: ### Related Issue **Issue:** #6192 ### Description Currently, orchestration is failing for requests to GPT-5 that include the `max_tokens` parameter (a future fix for orchestration will support GPT-5 with this deprecated parameter). This happens because the GPT-5 model family rejects the deprecated `max_tokens` parameter - only `max_completion_tokens` is accepted for reasoning models (such as GPT-5). More details can be found here: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5072518-controlling-the-length-of-openai-model-responses#h_930bf1dfa4 The original reason for adding the `max_tokens` parameter was to support the Anthropic model family. That issue was resolved a week ago, so this parameter is no longer required. If, in the future, we allow users to configure model parameters directly in the SAP AI Core provider, we will need to return the `model_params` field. ### Test Procedure - I tested that all models are working in orchestration mode ### Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [x] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots ### Additional Notes ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Remove `model_params` from `LlmModuleConfig` in `SapAiCoreHandler` to support GPT-5 models in orchestration mode. > > - **Behavior**: > - Remove `model_params` from `LlmModuleConfig` in `SapAiCoreHandler` to support GPT-5 models in orchestration mode. > - Addresses issue where GPT-5 models reject deprecated `max_tokens` parameter. > - **Misc**: > - Update changeset to reflect removal of `model_params` in orchestration mode. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=cline%2Fcline&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for aca82ce088a26b2218fdd8c05b7ea68d1f167cbe. issues.title: Kimi will truncate a long file when edit  cause max_token exceed.
issues.body: ### Plugin Type VSCode Extension ### Cline Version v3.28.6 ### What happened? When using the Kimi model provided by moonshot.cn to edit documents, if the output document length is too long, Kimi will truncate the document output and repeatedly retry the editing request. Based on local debugging results, this occurs because the maximum output length for the response has been reached. According to the documentation provided by Moonshot: https://platform.moonshot.cn/docs/guide/faq#kimi-api-%E8%BF%94%E5%9B%9E%E7%9A%84%E5%86%85%E5%AE%B9%E4%B8%8D%E5%AE%8C%E6%95%B4%E6%88%96%E8%A2%AB%E6%88%AA%E6%96%AD and https://platform.moonshot.cn/docs/api/chat#%E8%AF%B7%E6%B1%82%E5%86%85%E5%AE%B9 It can be concluded that when the request does not specify `max_tokens`, Kimi will use a default `max_tokens` value. If the model's required output length exceeds `max_tokens`, the model will truncate the output. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Select any model provided by moonshot.cn. 2. Requesting the model to generate or edit a large file (typically over 3000 characters), such as converting a large CSV file to a JSON file. 3. watching the model generate the file. ### Plugin Type

VSCode Extension
